# Q1 — which OCCT

**Pin OCCT 8.0.1.** It is the current release (published 2026-07-30) and the first maintenance release of
8.0; its notes say the C++17 API and ABI baseline set by 8.0.0p1 is unchanged, so a later 8.0.x is a
drop-in rebuild.

| | |
|---|---|
| Tag | `V8_0_1` (annotated tag object `c5605924864829ce8c1e1477f976ffb3880538a8`, commit `b8f597c677811d1f9f4d8a97f5ae2825c0353a42`) |
| Source archive | `https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT/archive/refs/tags/V8_0_1.tar.gz` — unpacks to `OCCT-8_0_1/` |
| SHA-256, as downloaded 2026-09-27 | `0d6913eae4bcc09a3653ceced6dda1aec11c35a1513d4c06762c9b002092c68a` (45,130,339 bytes) |
| Upstream checksum to compare against | **None for the source.** The GitHub release publishes SHA-256 digests for its eleven assets, all Windows/x64 binary and documentation zips (`opencascade-release-*.zip`, `3rdparty-vc14-64.zip`, `*-doc.zip`); the tag archive is generated by GitHub and carries no published digest |
| Licence files in the archive | `LICENSE_LGPL_21.txt`, `OCCT_LGPL_EXCEPTION.txt` (Q11) |
| Minimum CMake | 3.10 (`cmake_minimum_required (VERSION 3.10 FATAL_ERROR)`); built here with 4.4.3 |
| Minimum C++ | **C++17** (8.0.0: "Compilers below the C++17 line are no longer supported"); `BUILD_CPP_STANDARD` defaults to C++17 |

**The checksum is ours, not upstream's.** GitHub's generated archives have changed bytes before without the
content changing, so a mismatch on a later download is not by itself evidence of tampering — but it stops the
build, which is right. Brief 62 therefore records the commit hash beside the checksum, and the copy of the
archive retained to honour the LGPL written offer (brief 62 §6c; nothing is published while
[OCCT#1564](https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT/issues/1564) is open) is the one the recipe's checksum
names — so circuitRF never depends on GitHub regenerating it identically. A re-download on 2026-09-27
matched.

## What changed since 7.9 that the worker meets

From the 8.0.0 and 8.0.1 release notes (`https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT/releases/tag/V8_0_0`,
`…/V8.0.1`) and from compiling the harness:

- **C++17 minimum**; the source tree is `src/<Module>/<Toolkit>/<Package>/`. Nothing in the harness cared.
- **`Standard_Failure` derives from `std::exception`**; `Raise()`/`Throw()`/`Instance()` are gone (use `throw`),
  as are `Standard_ErrorHandler::Catches()`/`LastCaughtError()`. The worker catches `const Standard_Failure&`
  (or `std::exception`) and prints `ExceptionType()` and `what()` — Q9's output is that.
- **The error-handler stack is `thread_local`** and several TKBool globals became `thread_local`; 8.0.1 made
  fillet reconstruction re-entrant across threads. Relevant only if the worker ever runs operations
  concurrently; Q7 found serial and `SetRunParallel(true)` booleans byte-identical.
- **`occ::handle<T>`** is the spelling in every header; `Handle(T)` still compiles as a macro.
- **The `TopTools_*`, `TColStd_*` … collection typedefs** live under `src/Deprecated/NCollectionAliases/` and
  are deprecated; headers now speak `NCollection_IndexedMap<TopoDS_Shape, TopTools_ShapeMapHasher>` etc.
  The harness uses the `NCollection_*` spellings directly and so should the worker.
- **The OCCT math wrappers** (`Sqrt`, `Abs`, `Min`, …) are deprecated in favour of `std::`.
- **STEP moved into `TKDESTEP` at 7.8** (already so in 7.9): `STEPControl_*`, `STEPCAFControl_*` and the
  new **`DESTEP_Parameters`**, which carries the write unit and schema as fields (`WriteUnit`,
  `WriteSchema`) instead of `Interface_Static` strings. `STEPCAFControl_Writer::Perform(doc, file, params)`
  and `Transfer(doc, params)` take it directly (Q8).
- **Mesh algorithm plug-ins** register through `BRepMesh_DiscretAlgoFactory`; `BRepMesh_IncrementalMesh`
  is unchanged in use (Q10, Q12).
- **VTK is no longer on by default** — irrelevant here; the recipe turns every optional product off.
- 8.0.1 fixes that touch this series directly: a Boolean-section hang on periodic B-splines; several
  shape-healing crashes on missing pcurves; `ChFi3d_Builder::StartSol` hardened so an oversized chamfer
  returns `IsDone() == false` rather than crashing (Q9 saw the fillet equivalent); STEP export of oversized
  strings.

Nothing in the harness needed a deprecated API, and the build of the 25 configured toolkits produced **zero
compiler warnings** on either macOS architecture (`grep -c warning: build.log` → 0).
